answer.reason: The native terminal can draw on AMD Radeon Graphics (RADV NAVI14) (Vulkan)

findings: The shipping policy (CPU rasterizers refused) passed in the guest: wgpu found the host's Vulkan adapter, a RADV driver on a Navi 14, through the guest's Vulkan loader.
The probe cost 99 ms cold in a debug build, inside the 2 s budget; the page's own wait was 101 ms.

The answer did not list the adapters it saw and did not carry a device type: that is the probe of main before #2381. The case NativeTerminalCoreTest.theProbeRefusesASoftwareRasterizerUnlessTheDebugSwitchAllowsOne records both on the lane.
limits: Waydroid is the Android acceptance environment for the native-engine release (ADR 0001, Amendment 6). Its guest is x86_64 on the host GPU or a software rasterizer, so these timings are not a device result and every acceptedRisk below is not measured.

acceptedRisk.reason: Waydroid has no phone battery to read, so battery energy cannot be compared between engines.
Gboard and SwiftKey are not part of the guest unless installed and run; see vendorImesInstalled in the environment block and the guest IME.
The guest draws through the host GPU path or a software rasterizer, not a phone GPU driver.
Touches are injected events; a real digitizer, palm rejection and pressure are not exercised.
A workstation host does not throttle like a phone; sustained-load behaviour is unknown.
The guest is x86_64; the arm64 build that ships has not run here.
One WebView and one LineageOS-based image; vendor WebView and ROM variation are not covered.
